items.title: Forced dissipation and the exponential steady-state envelope

source.attribution: Mathlib supplies the one-sided Grönwall comparison; Samplinglib packages the forced energy-dissipation specialization used by semigroup and optimization arguments.

items.statement: For a continuous scalar energy with exact right derivative E'=-qD, a positive rate r and the inequality rE≤qD+b imply the sharp exponential interpolation E(t)≤E(s)e^{-r(t-s)}+(b/r)(1-e^{-r(t-s)}) for s≤t.
assumptions: The energy is continuous and has the supplied exact right derivative at every time.
The decay rate is strictly positive.
The forced coercivity inequality holds at every time.
The two endpoint times are ordered.

obligations.label: Derive the exact exponential envelope from right-derivative dissipation and forced coercivity

bindings.boundary: No concrete Markov semigroup, carré-du-champ derivative identity, curvature estimate, or generator-domain extension is asserted.

assumption_deltas.source: Mathlib's comparison theorem is stated for a continuous function with a right-slope upper bound f'≤Kf+ε on an interval.
assumption_deltas.lean: Samplinglib assumes a globally continuous `DissipationCurve`, its exact one-sided derivative E'=-qD, a globally stated forced coercivity inequality, r>0, and ordered endpoints.
assumption_deltas.reason: The exact derivative and coercivity data are the semigroup-facing adapter that produces Mathlib's slope hypothesis; positivity of r is necessary to write the forcing floor b/r. Global data match the existing reusable `DissipationCurve` API, while the proof uses them only on [s,t].
